findings.title: Localhost-only threat model brittle against real-world exposure vectors
findings.location: SDR-06-002: localhost-only. and Section 2. Design Decisions
findings.evidence: Binds to `http://127.0.0.1:7879`. No auth. Hackathon scope. ... threat model is "single-user local workstation." Post-hackathon: add authentication if multi-user.
findings.problem: Assumes perfect process isolation and no forwarding (ngrok, Docker, reverse proxies, shared dev machines, or firewall holes) while exposing full design history, session data, and a filesystem-derived screenshot endpoint.
findings.why_it_matters: If isolation assumption is false, sensitive IP leaks without any auth, logging, or rate limiting; retrofitting auth later cascades into every Razor page, JSON endpoint, and static handler already designed as unauthenticated.
findings.proposed_fix: Design all endpoints with pluggable auth from day one (even if flag-disabled for hackathon); explicitly enumerate and test boundary conditions under which the 7879 surface is considered safe.

findings.title: Rejection of real-time updates creates self-inflicted staleness and polling tax
findings.evidence: Specifically no WebSocket to the viewer — the existing WebSocket at :7878 is the add-in bridge, not a viewer push channel. Polling is sufficient for hackathon scope and avoids introducing a second WS endpoint.
findings.problem: The orchestrator already runs a real-time bridge on 7878 yet viewer deliberately chooses 3-second polling, guaranteeing delayed timeline during active modeling sessions the entire system exists to observe.
findings.why_it_matters: Violates the contrarian test "what if the opposite assumption (that polling is fine) is false?" — creates extra load, race conditions on new sessions, and UI lag precisely where immediacy matters most; hackathon excuse inflates long-term technical debt.
findings.proposed_fix: Reuse or extend the existing real-time channel (SSE is lighter than second WS) for viewer updates; remove the artificial "no second WS" rule and make live timeline baseline, not stretch.

findings.title: Deep validation can still produce unbounded HTTP request hangs
findings.location: SDR-06-005 and 5.3 GET /api/dhf/integrity?sessionId={uuid}&deep=false and 13. Failure Modes
findings.evidence: Deep validation (recomputes feature-tree hashes from JSONB and screenshot SHA-256s from files) runs only when the user hits `/api/dhf/integrity?deep=true`. ... The endpoint returns what's been validated so far with a truncation flag. No unbounded hangs.
findings.problem: No concrete timeout, cancellation token propagation, or max-duration guard is specified; "truncation flag" does not appear in the sample response schema; file I/O for screenshots scales with session size without bound.
findings.why_it_matters: A single deep=true request (or adversarial script) can stall the thread pool or render the viewer unusable exactly contrary to the stated goal of preventing page-load stalls; contradicts the shallow-by-default SDR.
findings.proposed_fix: Make deep validation an async background job returning a jobId for polling, or enforce hard 8-second timeout with partial results explicitly documented in the JSON contract.

findings.title: Project shape and test list already embed stretch features, undermining mandatory/stretch split
findings.evidence: Endpoints/ contains EntryDetailEndpoints.cs, IntegrityEndpoints.cs, ExportEndpoints.cs and Pages/ contains EntryDetail.cshtml even though SDR-06-004 declares them stretch. Required Tests lists PdfExportTests, ScreenshotPathTraversalTests.
findings.problem: The concrete folder layout, class names, and test inventory already assume the full feature set; "minimal is mandatory" is stated but not reflected in the scaffolding presented.
findings.why_it_matters: Creates scope drift and complexity inflation for a declared hackathon artifact; teams will implement everything because the spec already scaffolds it, defeating the explicit baseline-only intent.
findings.proposed_fix: Provide two distinct project shapes (MandatoryViewer/ vs Stretch/) and move all stretch tests and endpoints into a clearly gated follow-on spec or appendix.

top_3_must_fix: Localhost-only threat model brittle against real-world exposure vectors
Deep validation can still produce unbounded HTTP request hangs
Rejection of real-time updates creates self-inflicted staleness and polling tax
